key_insight: This baseline natural history study defines the first U.S. CADASIL cohort, showing how a single-gene small vessel disease model can be used to map clinical, cognitive, imaging, and biomarker variation relevant to VCID research.
clinical_relevance: The findings help establish standardized measures and reference data that may improve trial readiness and future biomarker-driven studies in hereditary and sporadic vascular cognitive impairment.
method: Cross-sectional baseline analysis from 12 U.S. sites (Oct 2022–Jan 2025).
Adults from families with documented NOTCH3 variants underwent harmonized clinical, cognitive, physical, MRI, genetics, and proteomics assessments.
Central genetic review classified pathogenic/likely pathogenic NOTCH3 variants into low-, medium-, or high-risk tiers.
evidence_signal: The analytic cohort included 343 CADASIL carriers and 116 non-carrier family controls, enabling group comparisons using nonparametric tests and multivariable adjustment.
watch_item: The cohort is predominantly White and highly educated, and baseline cross-sectional data cannot establish longitudinal disease progression or generalizability.
paper_title: The United States CADASIL Consortium: Baseline Findings from a Natural History Study
